about.headline: THE ADVANCED PACKAGE
copy: Mike Macdonald came to Seattle in 2024 from Baltimore, where his 2023 Ravens defense had led the league in points allowed, sacks and takeaways. By his second season in Seattle the defense was the {ppg|best in the league}, first in scoring at 17.2 points a game and first in DVOA.

They did it in two high shells with big nickel on the field, blitzing less than almost anybody and confusing protections instead: linebackers mugged in the A gaps, tackles dropping into coverage, the nickel coming free off the edge.

This is the advanced half of the defense that won Super Bowl LX {sb|29 to 13}, in three parts: the early down aggressive calls, the advanced coverages and the sim pressures. In Madden 27 it all runs out of the Arizona Cardinals playbook.

principles.title: STOP THE RUN ON EARLY DOWNS
principles.blurb: Win early downs, get them into obvious passing situations, then unleash the rest of the playbook.
principles.detail: Win early downs and the offense is in known passing situations, which is where every sim pressure and every zero in this package lives. The base calls stop the run from two high because the safeties are in the run fit, so the shell never changes and the box still gets loaded.

principles.title: CONFUSE THE PROTECTION
principles.blurb: Threaten six, rush four. The protection slides to a blitz that never comes and one of ours walks in free.
principles.detail: Threaten six and send four. The mugged linebackers and the walked up nickel make the protection slide, and then the ones they blocked for drop out while the nickel comes free. Seattle blitzed less than almost anybody in the league and still got home, because the front moves and the center never knows which four are coming.

principles.title: CREATE THE BIG PLAY
principles.blurb: Sacks, takeaways and touchdowns. This defense is built to end drives, not just get off the field.
principles.detail: Unblocked heat makes the quarterback throw early into a coverage with more defenders than receivers, and that is where the picks come from. The zeros get the sacks, the sims get the panicked throws, and the match coverage behind both is already sitting in the window.

playbook.note: In Madden 27 this whole defense runs out of the ARIZONA CARDINALS playbook. All three Seahawks installs do, so every call mixes and matches into one scheme.

jobs: MAN ON THE BACK SIDE OF BRACKET 9 SWITCH.
SOFT SQUAT AND FIRE DOWN ON THE RUN WITH THE MACRO ON.
DEEP THIRD BEHIND THE EDGE BLITZ.
MAN ACROSS THE BOARD ON THE ZERO.
MAN THE SLOT DOWN LOW UNDER THE BRACKET.
WALK DOWN ON FS WILL BLITZ 0.
SEAM FLAT: MATCH THE VERTICAL.
STEP IN FRONT OF THE CHECKDOWN.
PINCH INSIDE AND CONTROL THE A GAPS.

DROP INTO THE HOOK CURL ON OKIE EAGLE 3.
LOOP IN FREE WHEN THE LINE CHASES THE LOOPER.

SIT OVER THE CENTER ON THE ZERO, HOVER AND GET OUT.
THREE RECEIVER HOOK: EYES ON THE QUARTERBACK.

GO OUT WITH THE TACKLE SO THE LOOPER COMES FREE.
CONTAIN THE QUARTERBACK.
STEP UP, THEN DROP OUT AS THE USER ON THE SIMS.
LINE UP AT THE OUTSIDE END SPOT IN 3 HIGH OVER.
THREE HIGH BEFORE THE SNAP.
WALK DOWN AND COME ON THE ZERO.

stop.line: Every answer comes from the calls in this install and the Nickel: a coverage, a pressure and a change up where it fits, with the reason and the setup.

answers.name: Cover 4 Palms
answers.why: Palms is the call against three by one. Both corners are man everywhere he goes, the nickel and the trips safety read three to two, and the solo safety is a robber, so you always have backside help on crossers and deep digs.
answers.do: No setup. User the weak side safety and rove. The check is Stump.

answers.name: Bracket 9 Switch
answers.why: Against three by one the man side comes out on the trips, so flip it. Now it is Palms to the trips and man on the back side, and the user has no responsibilities at all.
answers.do: Flip the play so the match side is to the trips. User the safety doubled up over the slot.

answers.name: LB Blitz 6
answers.why: A five man pressure with match coverage behind it. The three players on the quarters side do a really good job matching two or three receivers, so that side goes to the trips.
answers.do: Blitz all linebackers. User the outside walked down linebacker, hover for half a second and get out.

answers.name: Cover 4 Palms
answers.why: Palms is the base call against bunch as well as trips. Bunch gets matched all across the field, and you are free over the middle when the backside number one breaks in.
answers.do: No setup. The check is Bingo. User the solo side safety.

answers.name: Bracket 9 Switch
answers.why: Bunch is the same thing as trips: flip it so the match is to the bunch, with man coverage on the back side.
answers.do: Flip the play so the match side is to the bunch. User the safety doubled up over the slot.

answers.name: Show SS Sim 2
answers.why: Flip it so the strong safety walks down on the bunch side. When they run the toss to the bunch he holds the edge, and on the pass he fires off the edge with only four rushing.
answers.do: Shift the D-line to the side the safety walked down on. QB contain. User the linebacker in the mid read.

answers.name: Cover 4 Quarters
answers.why: Quarters is the call against two by two. The corners take an outside quarter, the safeties read number two, and the nickel and the linebackers match underneath.
answers.do: No setup. User one of the two safeties and rove.

answers.name: Pounder
answers.why: Man underneath with the two safeties playing quarters over the middle of the field, the tight end and the slots, where people want to throw the ball anyway.
answers.do: User one of the high safeties and play him with quarters rules.

answers.name: Silver Shoot Pinch
answers.why: The first and ten call when you have no idea what they are running. If they send everybody out, the looper comes up the middle and the nickel comes off the edge, and both get there. The back decides who is free.
answers.do: Slant the D-line to the nickel and blitz all linebackers. User the linebacker on the nickel side: walk him down a step or two, do not blitz him. You have the back.

answers.name: Cover 4 Palms
answers.why: Palms against empty too. Empty is just three by two: two sets of rules on one call. Double team deep, and the out and up gets matched across the field.
answers.do: No setup. User a safety.

answers.name: Blitz Loop 3
answers.why: Five rushers, and if they do not block the running back it comes in every single time. In empty there is no back to block it. The seam flats match the verticals behind it.
answers.do: Shift the D-line to the blitz side and blitz all linebackers. User the outside standing linebacker: hover and get out.

answers.name: LB Pop 0
answers.why: If he sends everybody out on one of these, he has to get the football out in half a second. Empty sends everybody out.
answers.do: Shift the D-line away from the blitzing nickel and blitz all linebackers. You have whoever is uncovered.

answers.name: Run D Macro
answers.why: For heavy run users. Call it against anything that is not a spread look or doubles. The corners are in soft squats, so they are in the run fit and they drive down on the football right away.
answers.do: Call Quarters or Palms, then press L1 and call the macro. User a safety and be super aggressive.

answers.name: Show SS Sim 2
answers.why: The strong safety walks down and gives us a loaded box. Flip it so he is on the strength: the two tight end side, the wing side, whichever side has more players.
answers.do: Shift the D-line to his side. QB contain. User the linebacker in the mid read.

answers.name: Edge Blitz 3
answers.why: Three safeties down in the box and everybody in a run fit except the one in the deep blue. The pinched line controls the middle, which lets the linebacker loop in free on run plays a ton.
answers.do: Show blitz and pinch the D-line. User the middle high safety and be aggressive on the run.

answers.name: Cover 4 Palms
answers.why: It is built to take away everything trips offenses want: the corner routes and the flood concepts. The corner jumps the quick out and the safety takes number one over the top.
answers.do: No setup. User the weak side safety.

answers.name: SS Dog 3
answers.why: Four rushing and seven dropping. The seam flats match verticals from number two, and if your seam flat gets run off, you go help in the flat. Flood takes time, and the nickel is there as he hits the back of his drop.
answers.do: QB contain right away. User the linebacker on the blitz side: hover for half a second, then get out. Shade down to hard flats if he keeps taking the flat.

answers.name: Edge Blitz 3
answers.why: The pinched line controls the middle, which lets the linebacker loop in free on run plays a ton, and the safeties flow to the football.
answers.do: Show blitz and pinch the D-line. User the middle high safety.

answers.name: Run D Macro
answers.why: Everybody is coming downhill looking to make plays in the backfield. The goal is no gain or a loss, not four, five and six yard runs.
answers.do: Call Quarters, then the macro. User a safety.

answers.name: Bracket 9 Switch
answers.why: Everybody in man coverage is in a run fit, the safety is in a run fit and the nickel is in a run fit. The manned up corner fires down on the run and blows it up.
answers.do: Leave it as it comes out. Get aggressive with the user.

threats.name: Outside runs
threats.q: How do I stop outside runs?

answers.name: Show SS Sim 2
answers.why: The walked down safety holds the edge, the end scrapes over the top and the corners flow down. It shuts down outside runs.
answers.do: Flip it so the safety is on the strength and shift the D-line to him.

answers.name: FS Will Blitz 0
answers.why: Six across the line, basically a picket fence. It makes it very difficult to get outside in the run game.
answers.do: Pinch the D-line and user the linebacker down over the center. Hover and get out.

answers.name: Cover 4 Quarters
answers.why: All nine in the run fit out of Nickel 2-4. Safeties fire, linebackers fire, ends fire: string the run out and gang tackle it.
answers.do: No setup. User a safety and fire on it.

threats.name: Shotgun runs
threats.q: How do I stop shotgun runs?

answers.name: FS Zone Blitz
answers.why: Most shotgun runs go across the quarterback, so if the back is on the right the run goes left. Flip the play so the safety walks down away from the back, and you are playing the percentages.
answers.do: Flip it away from the back and walk the blitzing safety down beside the linebacker.

answers.name: FS Will Blitz 0
answers.why: Where it really excels against the run is controlling the edges: perimeter runs and shotgun runs are not getting outside.
answers.do: Pinch the D-line and user the linebacker down over the center.

answers.name: Cover 4 Quarters
answers.why: All nine in the run fit out of Nickel 2-4. As soon as they see run, everybody fires downhill: safeties fire, linebackers fire, ends fire.
answers.do: No setup. User a safety.

threats.name: First and ten
threats.q: What do I call on first and ten?

answers.name: Edge Blitz 3
answers.why: An early down aggressive call you can use against any opponent at any point in the game. It is meant to stop the run and play the pass equally, out of a look most people are not seeing.
answers.do: Show blitz, pinch the D-line, QB contain. User the middle high safety.

answers.name: Show SS Sim 2
answers.why: A base call you can make at any time: first and ten, second and ten. The walked down safety loads the box against the run, and on the pass it is a four man sim pressure with everybody else in coverage.
answers.do: Flip it so the safety is on the strength and shift the D-line to him. QB contain. User the linebacker in the mid read.

answers.name: Cover 4 Quarters
answers.why: One of the base calls in almost every scheme. It stops the run with all nine in the fit, it plays the pass with match rules, and the user has almost free rein to make plays on the back end.
answers.do: No setup. User one of the two safeties and rove.

threats.name: Third and short
threats.q: What do I call on third and short?

answers.name: FS Will Blitz 0
answers.why: The zero for third and inches, fourth and inches and fourth and short. Pinch the tackles into the A gaps with the linebacker down over the center and you control the interior, with six across the line.
answers.do: Pinch the D-line and user the linebacker down over the center. QB contain. Hover and get out: you have the back.

answers.name: Run D Macro
answers.why: For really obvious run situations. Everybody is coming downhill looking to make plays in the backfield, and the corners are in the run fit with them.
answers.do: Call Quarters or Palms, then press L1 and call the macro. User a safety and be super aggressive.

answers.name: Blitz Loop 3
answers.why: The pressure for when it has to come in. On third and two or fourth and three, shade down to hard flats and take away the quick hitters.
answers.do: Shift the D-line to the blitz side and blitz all linebackers. Shade down to hard flats. User the outside standing linebacker.

threats.name: Third and long
threats.q: What do I call on third and long?

answers.name: Okie Eagle 3
answers.why: Save this for fourth downs and third and longs where you know they are passing. Three rushing and eight dropping, one of the three comes in unblocked, and they have no idea what the picture is.
answers.do: QB contain. User the end away from the blitz: step up, then get out. Quick adjust the hard flat corner to a curl flat.

answers.name: Nickel Sim 2
answers.why: Second and long, third and long, fourth and long. An unblocked nickel off the edge while rushing only four, with seven dropping and playing off.
answers.do: Slide the D-line to the nickel and crash it down. User the backside end.

answers.name: 2 Invert Lurk
answers.why: On fourth and long: Coverage, then Play the Sticks. Now the flat defenders play at sixteen yards and nothing gets over their heads.
answers.do: User the high safety in the hook curl and keep him back. Coverage, then Play the Sticks.

threats.name: Red zone
threats.q: What do I call in the red zone?

answers.name: Run D Macro
answers.why: The base red zone call. It is Quarters with the corners in soft squats, so it still plays the pass and everybody is in the run fit.
answers.do: Call Quarters or Palms, then press L1 and call the macro. User a safety.

answers.name: Redzone DT Drop
answers.why: A four man sim with man across the board and both tackles dropping out under the quick hitters. The nickel comes free off the edge, and the tackles take the hot routes over the middle that man usually gives up.
answers.do: QB contain. User the outside linebacker on the line: hover and get out. You have whoever is uncovered.

answers.name: Cover 4 Quarters
answers.why: Match coverage with a four man rush. Number one goes vertical and the corner locks him up, number two goes vertical and the safety takes him. Double team deep, boxed, boxed.
answers.do: No setup. User one of the two safeties.

plays.name: Edge Blitz 3

reads.label: The Three High Look
reads.text: We start with a three high safety look, so we already have a unique look to the defense. It is very different from what most people are seeing, and it gives them a totally different picture to work out.

reads.label: The Looper Comes Free
reads.text: Everybody crashes inside. Three on two on the inside, both edges go out with the tackles, and the linebacker loops right up Main Street. Most of the time the looping blitzer comes in completely unblocked.

reads.label: A Tackle Loops In Too
reads.text: Sometimes the looping pressure forces the offensive linemen out of alignment and one of the D tackles loops in free as well, so there are two loopers right up the A gap in the quarterback's face. And sometimes they overshift inside, everyone squeezes down on the looper, and that lets the edge come free.

reads.label: Seam Flats Behind It
reads.text: Seam flats on the back end match the vertical routes, and the three receiver hook in the middle of the field has his eyes on the quarterback and steps in front. As the user in the deep blue you are expecting pressure: play the deep middle, and if you see something shallow, come meet it at the football.

reads.label: A Run Defense Too
reads.text: Three safeties down in the box, and everybody is in a run fit except the one in the deep blue. He is the user, so on a run you can be super aggressive. The pinched line controls the middle, which lets the linebacker loop in free on run plays a ton, and the safeties flow to the football and wipe it out.

adjustments: Show blitz: the safeties and the middle linebacker walk down
Pinch the D-line
QB contain
User the middle high safety, or the three receiver hook, it is up to you
Leave the seam flats on if you know how to use them, or shade up or down
plays.whenToUse: An early down aggressive call you can use against any opponent at any point in the game, so down and distance is kind of irrelevant. It is meant to stop the run and play the pass equally, get pressure and speed up the quarterback, out of a look most people are not seeing.

plays.name: FS Will Blitz 0

reads.label: Control the Middle
reads.text: Pinch the two D tackles into the A gaps, and with the linebacker user down over the center we control the interior of the offensive line.

reads.label: The Picket Fence
reads.text: The safety and the nickel walk down, so with the four D-linemen and the two walk down guys there are six across the line. It is basically a picket fence along the offensive line, and it makes it very difficult to get outside in the run game.

reads.label: Two Free off the Edge
reads.text: Hover and get out, and most of the time you get two free rushers coming off the edge at the quarterback. Sometimes it is just one and sometimes it is almost three, but the pressure comes from way outside very consistently.

reads.label: You Have Whoever Is Uncovered
reads.text: Zero man across the board. As the user you have the running back, or whoever is unguarded, sometimes a tight end. When the back stays in to block, you are free to help over the middle.

reads.label: Perimeter and Shotgun Runs
reads.text: Where it really excels against the run is controlling the edges: perimeter runs and shotgun runs are not getting outside. But there are not a lot of second level defenders, so if they are running I form lead straight downhill over and over, do not go to this.

adjustments: Pinch the D-line
User the linebacker in the middle of the field and bring him down over the center
QB contain
Blitz that linebacker too: you do not have to, it just helps hold the center
Hover and get out: you have the back or whoever is uncovered
plays.whenToUse: A great early down call because we can really control the line of scrimmage, and the zero for third and inches, fourth and inches and fourth and short. I do not run a ton of Cover 0 through the game, so when I do call it they are not expecting it.

plays.name: Bracket 9 Switch

reads.label: Half Man, Half Match
reads.text: Half the field in man, half the field in match. Match coverage to one side, man coverage to the other, and a three receiver hook in the middle looking for drags going to the man side.

reads.label: Against Two by Two, Leave It
reads.text: Any two by two set, any I form set, just leave it as it comes out. It is Quarters to the match side and man coverage on the back side.

reads.label: Against Trips and Bunch, Flip It
reads.text: Against any three by one set the man side comes out on the trips side, so flip the play and always have the match side to the trips. Now it is Palms to that side, and I love Palms against trips. Bunch is the same thing: flip it so the match is to the bunch. It works very well against empty too.

reads.label: You Are Completely Free
reads.text: User the safety in man coverage who is doubled up over the slot, and let the nickel man him up down low. You literally have no responsibilities: help on the man side, or on someone coming free from the match side. See the drag coming in late and drive on it.

reads.label: A Very Good Run Defense
reads.text: Everybody in man coverage is in a run fit, the safety is in a run fit and the nickel is in a run fit. Basically the only one who is not is the outside quarter corner. The manned up corner fires down on the run and blows it up, and you can get really aggressive with the user.

adjustments: No setup needed: it is a match coverage
Two by two or I form: leave it as it comes out
Three by one: flip the play so the match side is to the trips
Bunch: flip the play so the match side is to the bunch
User the safety in man coverage, the one doubled up over the slot
plays.whenToUse: One of my favorite coverages in the game so far. A blend of man and zone that can be an early down call and can work kind of anywhere, and because it is basically Quarters with everybody in a run fit it is a very good run defense too. Call it out of any formation that has it.

rulesLive.title: Bracket 9 Switch
rulesLive.intro: Half man, half match. The nickel side is man coverage, with the safety and the nickel doubling the slot. The other side is match: Quarters against two by two, and Palms against trips once you flip it. A three receiver hook sits between the two.

items.label: Half Man, Half Match
items.text: Any two by two set, leave it as it comes out. Man coverage to the nickel side and Quarters to the other side.

items.label: Man Side: the Corner
items.text: Man on number one, everywhere he goes.

items.label: Man Side: the Bracket
items.text: The nickel has the slot down low and the safety is doubled up over the top of him. That safety is your user, so let the nickel man him up and you are completely free.

items.label: Match Side: the Corner
items.text: Quarters rules. Man on demand, reading number one to number two: number one goes vertical and he locks him up, number one breaks in or stays shallow and he zones off to help on number two.

items.label: Match Side: the Safety
items.text: He reads number two to number one. Number two goes vertical and the safety plays him man. Number two breaks in or stays shallow and he scans to number one to bracket anything deep.

items.label: Match Side: the Quarter Flat
items.text: Cap number two if he releases vertical, then get eyes to the flat and take anything out there. Number two goes to the flat right away and he covers him.

items.label: The Three Receiver Hook
items.text: In the middle of the field, looking for the drags and anything else going to the man side.

items.label: Flip It: Match to the Trips
items.text: It comes out with the man side on the trips, so flip the play and always have the match side to the three. Now it is Palms to that side.

items.label: The Trips Corner
items.text: MEG on number one: man everywhere he goes. No switching and no passing off.

items.label: The Apex
items.text: He reads number three to number two. Number three goes fast to the flat and he takes him right away. Number three goes vertical or into the middle and he snaps his eyes to number two and mans him up.

items.label: The Trips Safety
items.text: He reads number three to number two. Number three goes vertical and the safety takes him. Number three stays shallow and number two goes vertical, and he picks up number two wherever he goes.

items.label: The Hook Walls Number Three
items.text: Wall off number three if he goes vertical or crosses, stay underneath him until the safety takes it, then look for the crossers.

items.label: The Back Side: You Are Free
items.text: The corner is in man on the one receiver, and the safety who was doubling the slot has nobody to double. You literally have no responsibilities: help on the back side, or on anything coming across from the trips.

plays.name: Run D Macro

reads.label: The Corners Join the Run Fit
reads.text: In normal match Quarters the corners are not in run fits: they play the pass first, backpedal, then come downhill and get wiped out of the play. With the macro on they are in soft squats, so they are in the run fit and they drive down on the football right away.

reads.label: Everybody Flies to the Football
reads.text: Super aggressive settings on the run, so everybody is coming downhill looking to make plays in the backfield. Every once in a while they overpursue. The goal is no gain or a loss, not four, five and six yard runs.

reads.label: Get Them in Third and Long
reads.text: The best way to beat a run player is to get him in third and fourth and longs: first and ten, second and ten, get some tackles for loss. Where you die to a runner is when he can consistently pick up four to five yards. I would rather play overly aggressive, and if they bust one on me, fine.

reads.label: The Soft Squat Against the Pass
reads.text: The soft squat is a match player. If number one goes vertical he matches him and turns into man coverage up the field. If number one goes in he plays the flat, and number two going out becomes the safety's job anyway. Everybody else is playing normal Quarters rules.

reads.label: The One Way It Gets Beat
reads.text: A slot receiver straight to the flat with number one going deep: the soft squat jumps the out and nobody takes the streak. If you are usering the safety on that side you can see it and jump it. Against somebody running the ball 80 percent of the time, giving that up once every five games is not the end of the world.

adjustments: Call Cover 4 Quarters or Palms: Nickel 2-4, or any front you like against the run
Press L1 and call the custom macro, wherever you saved it
The corners are now in soft squats and in the run fit
User a safety and be super aggressive
plays.whenToUse: For heavy run users, the ones who run the football 80 percent of the time, and for really obvious run situations. Call it against anything that is not a spread look or doubles. It still plays the pass, and it is the base red zone call too.

shot.label: The run defense macro
shot.how: Save it as a custom macro. Call Cover 4 Quarters or Palms, then press L1 and call it.

plays.name: Blitz DT Pop

reads.label: Only Four Rushing
reads.text: It is a sim pressure: we are only rushing four, because the two D tackles are actually going to drop out. One, two, three, four, and we are getting pressure.

reads.label: The Looper Comes Free
reads.text: The tackles do not drop right away, so they hold the inside. The edge crashes in and the looper comes all the way around free. Dexter Lawrence loops in free.

reads.label: Tackles in the Passing Lanes
reads.text: The D tackles drop into the quick passing lanes over the middle and take away the quick hitters, so he has to hold the football an extra half second. That is a D tackle forcing the incompletion.

reads.label: You Have the Running Back
reads.text: User the safety in man coverage on the running back. He is usually the easiest cover, and if the back blocks you are free to help over the middle: see it, drive on the football, step in front for the pick.

reads.label: Sound Even When It Is Blocked
reads.text: It is not guaranteed pressure every time. But if it turns into a four man rush, that is no different from running a normal four man rush anyway, and we are so sound on the back end that it does not really matter.

adjustments: Put a defensive end at the outside end spot, not a third D tackle: he comes in faster
Show blitz
QB contain
User the safety in man coverage on the running back
On obvious passing downs: user one of the D tackles instead, blitz him, then hover and get out yourself
plays.whenToUse: A four man sim pressure out of the three high look: the tackles drop into the middle, the looper comes around free, and it is man coverage behind it. On third down when you know they are passing, user a D tackle and it comes in even better.

plays.name: Okie Eagle 3

reads.label: A Three Man Sim Pressure
reads.text: Most sim pressures rush four. This one rushes three and gets home an absolute ton. One side of the field has no rushers at all: it is these three players against five offensive linemen, and one of them comes in unblocked.

reads.label: Everybody Else Drops
reads.text: The whole defense rotates over on the auto walk down, the D tackle drops into a hook curl and the end you are usering drops out too. Look at how many guys we have out in coverage: three rushing and eight dropping.

reads.label: The Rotated Cover 3
reads.text: A rotated Cover 3 on the back end with an inverted look on one side of the field. He tries to get up the seam and throws it right into the inverted Cover 3.

reads.label: Curl Flat or Hard Flat
reads.text: The corner on the blitz side comes out in a hard flat. Most of the time, quick adjust him to a curl flat so there are matching curl flats on both sides and he gets vertical under the out route. On third or fourth and short, leave the hard flat on the field.

reads.label: Step Up, Then Get Out
reads.text: User the defensive end away from the blitz. At the snap take a step up, then get out and play across the middle of the field. Even if you get caught and it turns into a four man sim pressure, that is all good.

adjustments: QB contain
User the defensive end who is rushing away from the blitz
At the snap take a step up, then get out
Quick adjust the hard flat corner to a curl flat, unless it is short yardage
plays.whenToUse: For obvious passing downs. Save this for fourth downs and third and longs where you know they are passing, the huge down where you need to confuse them and they have no idea what the picture is. Against a shotgun run you should be okay, but this is the one you call when you really want to make a statement.

plays.name: Edge Blitz 2

reads.label: The Same Blitz as Edge Blitz 3
reads.text: The identical play as Edge Blitz 3 with a Cover 2 shell behind it. The same interior look, the same looping pressure from the linebacker.

reads.label: Somebody Comes Free
reads.text: The linebacker comes free, or the looping creates issues for the linemen in the middle and a D tackle comes free too. When they pinch their protection inside to take away the looper, the edge comes in unblocked.

reads.label: Soft Squats Outside
reads.text: The soft squats match number one deep, then look to number two, or they trap the flat and send number two off to the safety or the vert hook. You get a double at the catch point.

reads.label: The User in the Vert Hook
reads.text: User the middle safety. He is one of the two vert hooks, so go out to his side of the field. The vert hooks match all the way across the field.

reads.label: Still a Run Defense
reads.text: It can still stop the run. Not quite as good against the run as the Cover 3 version, but still a solid run defense.

adjustments: Show blitz
Pinch the D-line
QB contain
User the middle safety in the vert hook
Leave the soft squats on, or shade down for hards, or shade up for clouds
plays.whenToUse: The Cover 2 version of Edge Blitz 3. The same setup and the same looping pressure with a different shell behind it, so you can change the picture on the back end without changing the blitz.

plays.name: FS Zone Blitz

reads.label: Four on Three
reads.text: On the blitz side we are creating a four on three. One takes the center, one takes the tackle, and the guard has to pick between the linebacker and the safety. He cannot take both, so one of them comes free.

reads.label: Walk the Safety Down
reads.text: The free safety comes from depth, so it takes a tiny bit long. Walk him down beside the linebacker yourself, and now either him or the linebacker comes free and it happens a lot quicker.

reads.label: Seam Flats and the Deep Middle
reads.text: Seam flats on the field match the vertical routes. User the middle high safety and play the middle of the field. Matched, matched, matched, and the three receiver hook gets underneath the quick throw.

reads.label: Against Shotgun Runs
reads.text: Most shotgun runs go across the quarterback's body, so if the back is on the right the run goes left. Flip the play so the safety walks down away from the back, and you are playing the percentages. To the same side it is still solid, because we are overloading that side and the linebacker and the safety are coming downhill so hard.

adjustments: In shotgun, flip the play so the safety walks down on the side away from the running back
QB contain
User the deep safety, or the three receiver hook
Walk the blitzing safety down beside the linebacker
Leave the seam flats on, or shade up or down
plays.whenToUse: Another early down aggressive call. Really good against people who play a lot of shotgun, when it is early and they could run or pass. I do not love it against I form or a ton of tight ends.

plays.name: Cover 6 Press

reads.label: A Three Man Rush
reads.text: This Cover 6 only rushes three, so there is an extra hook curl in the middle of the field with basically no responsibilities. He is just free, and that is who I user.

reads.label: A Curl Flat, Not a Quarter Flat
reads.text: The other difference is a curl flat on the field instead of a quarter flat, so you have to be a little careful with some of the match stuff.

reads.label: Match All Across the Field
reads.text: Match coverage across the board, and we meet at the catch point: double coverage down the field, a triple team on the drag, the three receiver hook stepping in front. A lot of people have no idea how to attack match, especially a variation like this.

reads.label: The Blitz out of It
reads.text: Blitz all linebackers, slant the line away from the vert hook and blitz the vert hook, and it is a five man blitz where either the linebacker or the vert hook comes free. The soft squat still plays as a soft squat and the quarter players and the curl flat are still there, so it is match coverage behind a blitz.

reads.label: The User on the Blitz
reads.text: On the blitz, user the linebacker away from the blitzing vert hook and walk him down so he mugs the gap. Then step underneath the throw.

adjustments: As a coverage: no setup, user the free hook curl
For the blitz: blitz all linebackers
Slant the D-line away from the vert hook, who is on the same side as the soft squat
Blitz the vert hook
User the linebacker away from the blitzing vert hook and walk him down to mug the gap
plays.whenToUse: A version of Cover 6 with a three man rush and an extra free player in the middle, and a blitz you can run out of the same look. You can run Cover 6 out of anything. This one is here for the wrinkle: match coverage on the back end with five coming.

rulesLive.title: Cover 6
rulesLive.intro: Cover 6 is two coverages in one call: Quarters to one side of the field and Cover 2 to the other. Quarter, quarter, half. The Quarters side goes to the passing strength and plays the match rules you already know. The Cover 2 side is a soft squat corner, a vert hook and a deep half safety.

items.label: Quarter, Quarter, Half
items.text: Quarters to the nickel side, Cover 2 to the other side. Two deep quarters and a deep half over the top, and the receivers are numbered outside in on each side, the same as always.

items.label: Quarters Side: the Corner
items.text: Man on demand, reading number one to number two. Number one goes vertical and he locks him up in man. Number one breaks in or stays shallow and he zones off, looking to help on number two.

items.label: Quarters Side: the Safety
items.text: He reads number two to number one. Number two goes vertical and the safety plays him man: streaks, corners, posts. Number two breaks in or stays shallow and he scans to number one to bracket anything deep.

items.label: Quarters Side: the Quarter Flat
items.text: Cap number two if he releases vertical, then get eyes to the flat and take anything out there. Number two goes to the flat right away and he covers him.

items.label: The Three Receiver Hook
items.text: Mostly free against two by two, with no locked in man. He helps over the middle, picks up the crossers and takes the second player to the flat.

items.label: Cover 2 Side: the Soft Squat
items.text: The corner is a match player. Number one releases outside and goes vertical, and he matches him and turns into man coverage up the field. Number one comes inside and number two goes straight to the flat, and he traps the flat and takes number two.

items.label: Cover 2 Side: the Vert Hook
items.text: He reads number two to number one. Number two goes vertical and he carries him up the seam. Number two goes to the flat with number one coming inside, and he takes number one. They swap.

items.label: Cover 2 Side: the Deep Half
items.text: No match rules. He plays the deep half and caps the vertical on his side, so when the soft squat runs with number one there is a double at the catch point.

items.label: Trips to the Quarters Side
items.text: The three receiver side gets the Quarters side, and against trips that side plays the Palms rules. The Cover 2 side is left on the one receiver.

items.label: The Trips Corner
items.text: MEG on number one: man everywhere he goes. Vertical, inside, across the field, it does not matter. No switching and no passing off.

items.label: The Apex and the Safety
items.text: Both read number three to number two. Number three goes fast to the flat and the apex takes him, and if number two is vertical the safety has him. Number three goes vertical and the safety takes him, and the apex snaps his eyes to number two and mans him up.

items.label: The Hook Walls Number Three
items.text: Wall off number three if he goes vertical or crosses. Stay underneath him until the safety takes it, then drift back into space and look for the crossers and the digs.

items.label: The One Receiver Side
items.text: The soft squat is on the lone receiver with the deep half safety over the top of him. That safety only has the deep half, which makes him the one to user.

plays.name: Mike SS 3 Seam

reads.label: Four Rushing, Four on Three
reads.text: Only four rushing: the D tackle in the middle and a three man rush on the outside. But it is a four on three to that side, and we are still dropping an extra guy out. That is my kind of math.

reads.label: One of the Three Comes Home
reads.text: One, two, three on that side, and if they only block five, one of them comes home basically every single time. Even when they block the back and it is four on six, the looper still gets free.

reads.label: Hover, Then Get Out
reads.text: User the defensive end away from the sim pressure. Hover, then get out and play over the middle of the field. He feels the pressure, tries to get the quick one out, and you meet it.

reads.label: Seam Flats Match It
reads.text: Seam flats on the field match the vertical routes. He checks it down in the flat and Witherspoon steps in front for the pick six. On short yardage you can always shade down.

reads.label: Sound Even When It Is Late
reads.text: Even if it does not come in clean, we are still only rushing four, so we are not losing anything on the back end. We are still playing a really sound coverage and still taking a ton of things away.

adjustments: QB contain
User the defensive end away from the sim pressure
Hover, then get out and play the middle of the field
Leave the seam flats on, or shade down, or shade up for curls, clouds or hards: it will not affect the blitz
plays.whenToUse: Another sim pressure to add to the two from the video, and it is insanely easy to set up. Four rushing, a four on three off the edge, and a sound Cover 3 with seam flats behind it.

plays.name: Seam Flats and Zone Blitzes
plays.whenToUse: Seam flats are the purple zones on the edge of every zone blitz in this defense. They are match defenders: after the snap they turn into man coverage on number two when he threatens them. That is why they are worth leaving on the field, and why you have to know what they will and will not take.

rulesLive.title: Seam flats
rulesLive.intro: Seam flats are the purple zones on the edge of every zone blitz in this defense. They are match defenders: after the snap they turn into man coverage on number two when he threatens them. That is why they are worth leaving on the field, and why you have to know what they will and will not take.

items.label: Three deep, three under
items.text: Every zone blitz in this defense has the same six behind it: three deep thirds, two seam flats and one three receiver hook. It is Cover 3 Match with one fewer man underneath, because he is coming.

items.label: He reads number two
items.text: Count from the outside in. Number one is the outside receiver, number two is the next man in. Each seam flat has his eyes on number two to his side, and what number two does decides what he becomes.

items.label: Two goes vertical
items.text: He turns into man coverage and carries him up the seam. This is the one that wins: he tries to go up the seam, the seam flat matches it and takes it away.

items.label: Two goes out
items.text: An out or a quick throw to the flat from number two, and he matches that too, from outside leverage.

items.label: Two goes inside
items.text: A slant or a drag by number two is not his. He lets it go to the middle of the field, where the three receiver hook is waiting, and zones off to the flat.

items.label: Number one stays short
items.text: When number one hitches or breaks under, the picture changes: the seam flat sinks under number one, and the corner in the deep third takes number two on the corner route.

items.label: The corners
items.text: Deep thirds, on top of number one. With the seam flats carrying number two, all four verticals have a man on them.

items.label: The middle third
items.text: The middle safety is the roof. If you user him you are expecting pressure: play the deep middle, and if you see something shallow, come meet it at the football.

items.label: The three receiver hook
items.text: His first steps are toward number three. He is the only help in the middle of the field: eyes on the quarterback, he walls the crosser and steps in front of the quick throw.

items.label: Where it gets hit
items.text: Number two goes vertical and takes the seam flat with him, and the flat behind him is open: curl flat, comeback flat, flood. If you are the user and your seam flat gets run off, go help in the flat.

items.label: Short yardage
items.text: Shade down and the seam flats become hard flats, so the quick throws to the flat get wiped out. You give up the match on the seam to get it. Shade up for curl flats or clouds. None of it changes the blitz.

items.label: The count changes
items.text: Against trips there are three to one side and one to the other. The trips side seam flat still reads number two. The three receiver hook now has a real number three, the inside receiver, and his first steps go to him. The back side seam flat has no number two, so the back is his.

items.label: Three verticals
items.text: The corner is on top of number one and the seam flat carries number two, the same as always. Number three is the hook's: he walls him and stays underneath until the middle third takes him over the top.

items.label: The flood
items.text: Number one clears out, number two runs the corner or the out and takes the seam flat with him, and number three goes to the flat. That flat is the throw against this. User the three receiver hook and go with number three, or shade down to hard flats.

items.label: The back side
items.text: One receiver, one corner on top of him. The seam flat reads the back: if he releases, he takes him, and if he stays in to block, he sinks under number one.

plays.name: Cover 4 Quarters

reads.label: Quarters Against Two by Two
reads.text: Rotate through Quarters and Palms as the base. Quarters is the call against two by two, even sets: both corners take an outside quarter, both safeties an inside quarter and read number two, and the nickel and the linebackers match underneath. The full rules are on the site and in the two college deep dives, and they are the same in Madden.

reads.label: User a Safety and Rove
reads.text: Always user one of the two safeties. Once the match rules have everybody else accounted for, you are basically free, roving and helping on anything you see: the deep crosser comes across, you take it, and the other safety steps down to disrupt the throw into his window.

reads.label: All Nine in the Run Fit
reads.text: The front four, the nickel, both linebackers and both safeties are all in run fits out of Nickel 2-4. As soon as they see run, everybody fires downhill: safeties fire, linebackers fire, ends fire. It is just a great run defense.

reads.label: Everything Boxed, Four Rushing
reads.text: Double team deep, boxed, boxed, and still a four man pressure with the front four. He tries to throw it on the run and there are two of ours at the catch point. That freedom on the back end is why match is the base.

reads.label: Against Bunch, the Box Check
reads.text: Quarters against bunch is the Box check, on the Cover 4 checks sheet. Later Seahawks installs go deeper on bunch and the other odd sets.

adjustments: No setup needed
User one of the two safeties
Rotate it with Palms: Quarters against two by two, Palms against three by one
Against bunch: the Box check
plays.whenToUse: One of the base calls in almost every scheme, because it is the most adaptable way to play defense in Madden and college football. It stops the run with all nine in the fit, it plays the pass with match rules, and once you understand how it works the user has almost free rein to make plays on the back end. Call it against two by two.

rules.title: Cover 4 Quarters
rules.intro: These are the rules for match coverage, not a formation. They travel: any scheme, any front you are lined up in can play them, and the numbering never changes.

shots.t: Quarters vs bunch, the box check
shots.img: art/Bama Assets__Quarters Vs Bunch Screen Shot.webp

b: #1 is the outside receiver.
#2 is the next man in, slot or tight end.
#3 only shows up on trips.
Reads run outside in.

sections.t: The corner: MOD, man on demand, reads #1 to #2
b: #1 goes vertical (five yards or more) and he locks him up in man.
#1 breaks in or shallow and he zones off, looking to help on #2. If #2 runs a corner or a streak he doubles him.
Both stay short and he sinks back into the deep quarter.
#2 goes vertical and the safety plays him man. Streaks, corners, posts.
#2 breaks in or shallow and he scans to #1 to bracket anything deep.
Both stay shallow and he is free help over the middle, doubling crossers from the other side.

sections.t: The quarter flat: nickel or apex
b: Cap #2 if he releases vertical, then get eyes to the flat and take anything out there.
#2 goes flat right away and he covers him.
#2 runs a wheel and he matches it upfield, converting to man.
No flat threat and he buzzes under any dig or curl behind him.
On a drag: away from the back he carries it across. On the back's side he passes it to the three receiver hook.

sections.t: The three receiver hook: the free man
b: In 2x2 he is mostly free, with no locked in man assignment.
His job is to help over the middle and pick up crossers or late flat routes.
He takes the second player to the flat: once the quarter flat gets run off, the next one out there is his.
A floater. He doubles crossers, jumps underneath routes and cleans up the space the quarter flat cannot reach.
Corners, crossers, deep posts. Quarters takes every one of them away.
The corners play man on demand, so nothing gets in behind them.
The safeties read and close on anything vertical.
Double teams sit at the catch point, out of a two high shell that tells the offense nothing.
Still match coverage, not a spot drop. Matched by quadrant, not by receiver number.
Corner takes the first one deep and outside, safety the first one deep and inside.
Quarter flat takes the first one shallow and outside, three receiver hook the first one shallow and inside.
Nobody starts with a man. Everybody starts with a direction.
Backside: the corner plays man everywhere on the solo receiver, the backside quarter flat mans up the back if he releases, and the backside safety is the one you user, free to help on anybody.
The exact same box check with one change: the corner locks onto #1 in man if he stays outside, instead of reading his quadrant.
Tested against every variation of flood and it holds. This is the adjustment to use against bunch.

films.t: Quarters vs bunch, the box check

plays.name: Cover 4 Palms

reads.label: Palms Against Three by One
reads.text: The other half of the rotation. Palms is the call against three by one: the same two high shell as Quarters, the same numbering, with the corner and the safety reading number two together. The full rules are on the site and in the two college deep dives, and they are the same in Madden.

reads.label: User the Weak Side Safety
reads.text: Against three by one, user the weak side safety, because now you are basically free, roving and looking to help on anything you see. Against bunch, user the solo side safety: bunch gets matched all across the field and you are free over the middle when the backside number one breaks in.

reads.label: Empty and the Out and Up
reads.text: Palms against empty too. Double team deep, the out and up gets matched across the field, and there is nowhere to go. He throws the deep corner route, Nick Emmanwori is step for step, click on and high point it for the pick.

reads.label: The Same Run Fit
reads.text: The same nine in the fit as Quarters: safeties fire, linebackers fire, ends fire. String the run out and gang tackle it.

reads.label: The Checks
reads.text: Palms against bunch is Bingo, against trips it is Stump, and against a one receiver side with a tight end it is Solo Cut. They are all on the Cover 4 checks sheet.

adjustments: No setup needed
Against three by one, user the weak side safety and rove
Against bunch, user the solo side safety
Rotate it with Quarters: Palms against three by one and empty
Checks: bunch is Bingo, trips is Stump, one receiver tight is Solo Cut
plays.whenToUse: The base call against three by one, and against empty as well. Rotate it with Quarters so the picture stays the same and the rules change, and use the free safety to make plays on the back end. Later Seahawks installs go deeper on bunch and the other odd sets.

rules.title: Cover 4 Palms
rules.intro: Palms is the trips call. The same two high shell as Quarters, the same numbering, and the corner and the safety read together so the flat gets jumped and the deep stuff gets doubled. Against empty it is two sets of rules in one call.

shots.img: art/Bama Assets__Palms Vs Trips Screen Shot.webp
art/Bama Assets__Palms Vs Empty Screen Shot.webp

b: #1 is always the outside receiver.
#2 is the next man in, slot or tight end.
#3 is the inside most man in the trips.
Everything counts outside in.

sections.t: The trips corner: MEG, man everywhere he goes
b: MEG on #1. Man everywhere he goes, no exceptions.
Vertical, inside, across the field, it does not matter. He travels.
No switching and no passing off. This is pure man.

sections.t: The nickel or apex on the trips side: reads #3 to #2
b: #3 goes fast to the flat (arrow, whip, quick out) and he takes him right away, matching him to the flat and running with him.
#3 goes vertical or into the middle (five yards or more, seam or crosser) and he snaps his eyes to #2 and mans him up.
Once he is on #2 he takes him anywhere on the field, short or deep.
#3 goes vertical and the safety takes him. Seam, post, corner, anything vertical.
#3 stays shallow and #2 goes vertical and he picks up #2 and takes him wherever he goes.
Both #2 and #3 stay shallow and he is free help over the top, usually doubling #1 on a post or a deep dig.
First rule: wall off #3 if he goes vertical or crosses. Stay underneath him until the safety takes it, then drift back into space.
If the back is already taken by the apex and somebody else comes into that flat late, the Mike picks him up.
Otherwise he sits in the middle, reads the quarterback and looks for crossers and digs.

sections.t: The solo apex: quarter flat, man on the back
b: He has the running back. Swing, angle or wheel, it is man everywhere he goes.
If the back stays in to block he sits in the flat, watches for late releases and drives on checkdowns.

sections.t: The solo safety: the robber, your user
b: This is the free player. He is your robber and he can help anywhere.
#1 on his side goes vertical and he brackets him with the corner.
#1 breaks inside or shallow and he looks back across the field to help on crossers from the trips side.
That back side help on crossers and deep digs is what makes Palms elite.
MEG on #1. Man everywhere he goes.
If the solo side is an inline tight end instead of a receiver: vertical or a corner route and he takes him man.
If that tight end breaks inside, the safety takes him across and this corner looks for work from the trips side.

sections.t: Against empty: two sets of rules, one call
b: Empty is just 3x2. The trips side plays straight Palms, counting 3 to 2. The two receiver side plays Palms against 2x2 and traps the flat.
Nobody is holding a back, so everybody is on a receiver.
The two receiver side corner sits on #2 to the flat instead of bailing. That is the trap: quick outs and flat routes get jumped, and the safety takes #1 over the top the second the corner drives.
#2 and #1 both vertical and both defenders lock on in man. #2 runs a wheel and the corner carries him and converts to man.
If one side has an inline tight end instead of a true slot, that side plays standard Quarters: corner in MOD on #1, safety reading #2 to #1, apex jamming #2 and taking the first man to the flat.
Takes away the corner routes and flood concepts trips lives on.
You still get a free robber on the back side.
Two high shell, so it gives up nothing pre snap.
Still fits the run with the safeties.

plays.name: Show SS Sim 2

reads.label: Stop the Run and Play the Pass
reads.text: A base call has to do both. The strong safety walks down and gives us a loaded box on the run, and on the pass he fires off the edge as a four man sim pressure with everybody else dropping out. Super balanced, so it can be called on any down.

reads.label: Only Four Rushing
reads.text: One, two, three, four. The safety comes unblocked off the edge and he is there by the time the quarterback hits the back of his drop. Even when they block it up, which they will sometimes, we are still dropping everybody else into coverage.

reads.label: The Deep Cloud Flats
reads.text: The corners sit in deep cloud flats, so when he tries to throw it up over our heads the safety and the corner meet at the football.

reads.label: The User Over the Middle
reads.text: You are in the mid read, sitting in the gap between the end and the tackle on the blitz side. Anything over the middle, step in front of it. Ernest Jones took one back for six on fourth and seven.

reads.label: The Run Fit
reads.text: The walked down safety is on the strength, so when they run the toss to the bunch side he holds the edge, the end scrapes over the top and the corners flow down. It shuts down outside runs, and it gets good sheds inside when they run it up the middle.

adjustments: When you break the huddle the strong safety often walks down on the weak side: flip the play so he is on the strength, the two tight end side, the bunch side, the wing side, whichever side has more players
Against a two by two set with no strong side, you do not have to flip it
Shift the D-line to the side the safety walked down on
QB contain
User the linebacker in the mid read and stay down in the gap between the end and the tackle on that side
plays.whenToUse: A base call you can make at any time in the game: first and ten, second and ten, even fourth and seven. It does both jobs, the walked down safety loads the box and holds the edge against the run, and on the pass it is a four man sim pressure with unblocked heat and everybody else in coverage.

plays.name: Silver Shoot Pinch

reads.label: Two Free Rushers
reads.text: If they send everybody out, the looping linebacker comes up the middle and the nickel comes off the edge, and both get there. Super fast pressure. Against play action it was four free rushers in on Mahomes.

reads.label: The Back Decides Who Is Free
reads.text: If the back stays in, he usually blocks the looper and the nickel is free. If he shoots out to the nickel, the looper is free. Either way the ball has to be out right now.

reads.label: You Have Whoever Is Uncovered
reads.text: Man across the board, and the user has the running back or the tight end, whoever nobody is locked on. Back goes out on a swing, run out with him. Back stays in, you are free to help over the middle on the tight end or the post.

reads.label: A Run Defense Too
reads.text: With everybody flying to the football this holds up against the run. Not the best run defense in the package, but it is a first and ten call when you have no idea what they are running.

adjustments: Slant the D-line to the side the nickel is blitzing from
Blitz all linebackers
User the linebacker on the same side as the nickel
Do not blitz him: walk him down one or two steps into the gap between the tackles
You have the back or whoever is uncovered in man
plays.whenToUse: The zero pressure with two free rushers when they send everybody out, and super fast pressure when they do not. With everybody flying to the football it works like a base call too, so you can call it on first and ten when you are not sure what they are running.

plays.name: LB Blitz 6

reads.label: Blitzing With Match Coverage
reads.text: A Cover 6 shell on the back end behind a five man pressure. We are relying on the heat to get there, and if they keep extra guys in to block, the coverage is good enough to hold.

reads.label: Look to the Cover 2 Side First
reads.text: The three players on the quarters side do a really good job matching two or three receivers, so as the user open up to the Cover 2 side first. Nothing there, shoot your eyes back to the quarters side.

reads.label: Unblocked off the Edge
reads.text: When they send everybody out, the pressure comes unblocked on the side away from the user. Hover for half a second and get out over the middle.

reads.label: When It Gets Blocked Up
reads.text: They block the back and it gets picked up. Fine. Now you are in the middle of the field looking for who is not getting matched. He tries the quick throw over the middle and a match defender steps right in front of it.

adjustments: Shift the D-line away from the side the two walked down linebackers are on
Slant the D-line out
Blitz all linebackers
User the outside one of the two walked down linebackers
If it is not coming in, try QB contain with the same setup
plays.whenToUse: The blitz that keeps match coverage behind it. It does not come in every single time, but it is only a five man pressure with such good coverage on the back end that it is really effective, and a picked up blitz does not turn into a big play.

plays.name: SS Dog 3

reads.label: Four Rushing, Seven Dropping
reads.text: The user hovers for half a second so the tackle has to respect him and bite inside, then gets out. That is what lets the nickel come unblocked off the edge. One, two, three, four rushing, seven dropping out, unblocked pressure as he hits the back of his drop.

reads.label: The Three Receiver Hook Is a Tackle
reads.text: It is not just linebackers dropping in this defense. A defensive tackle drops out into the three receiver hook here. Byron Murphy saw the drag coming across and stepped in front for the pick on fourth and eight.

reads.label: The Seam Flats Match
reads.text: The seam flats match verticals from number two. With you and the three receiver hook in the middle, you play over the middle unless number two goes to the flat, and if your seam flat gets run off, go help in the flat. Witherspoon stepped in front of one for a huge pick.

reads.label: They Block the Back
reads.text: If they keep the back in, they can block it up. Fine, because we can still get sheds, and now it is seven on four on the back end. Shade down to hard flats and the quick throws to the flat get wiped out: Witherspoon took one for six.

adjustments: QB contain right away
User the linebacker on the same side as the blitzing nickel
Do not blitz him: hover for half a second so the tackle bites inside, then get out
Seam flats stay on; shade down to hard flats to take away the quick throws to the flat
plays.whenToUse: A sim pressure, the kind Mike Macdonald runs a lot of: four rush, seven drop, and unblocked heat off the edge once the tackle bites inside. Any time you want pressure without giving up the numbers on the back end.

plays.name: Redzone DT Drop

reads.label: Four Rush, Unblocked Edge
reads.text: One, two, three, four come and the nickel comes free off the edge basically every time they send everybody out. Even when they block the back, six on four, the nickel still comes unblocked.

reads.label: The Tackles Drop Out
reads.text: Both defensive tackles drop into hook curls under the quick hitters, which is the weirdest look for people to attack. Byron Murphy under a post for the knockdown, Leonard Williams at six foot six skying up to swat one.

reads.label: Man Across the Board
reads.text: Man coverage everywhere behind it, so you need guys who hold up one on one and make plays on the ball. The tackles take the hot routes over the middle that man usually gives up.

reads.label: You Have Whoever Is Uncovered
reads.text: As the user you have whoever is uncovered in man. A lot of the time that is the running back out of trips or bunch, sometimes a slot or a tight end. Know who it is before the snap.

adjustments: QB contain
User the outside one of the two linebackers on the line, beside the defensive end
Hover and get out; you have whoever is uncovered in man
plays.whenToUse: Incredibly easy to set up and a totally different wrinkle: a four man sim with man across the board and both tackles dropping out under the quick hitters. Really good pressure, and a look people do not know how to attack.

plays.name: Nickel Sim 2

reads.label: Unblocked Nickel off the Edge
reads.text: The whole point of a sim pressure: we get home with four. Slide the line to the nickel and crash it down, and the nickel comes free off the edge while the backside end drops out. Hit before he can hit the back of his drop.

reads.label: Only Four Rushing
reads.text: One, two, three, four. The user on the backside is free to play over the middle, so it is three defenders in the middle of the field plus the deep shell. The numbers advantage in the secondary is massive.

reads.label: When They Block the Back
reads.text: Block the back and it is six blocking four. Sometimes that blocks it up, and sometimes it still comes in. Because we outnumber them so badly on the blitz side, sometimes the end shoots out and the nickel loops inside. Max protect it and they only have three out on routes against our seven.

reads.label: Off Coverage on Long Yardage
reads.text: Third and twenty seven, fourth and thirteen: our guys are playing off, seven dropping into coverage. He throws it up and the flat defender steps in front for the pick.

adjustments: Slide the D-line to the blitzing nickel
Crash the D-line down
User the backside defensive end, away from the blitz
Cloud flats stay on the field, shade down to hard flats if you want
plays.whenToUse: A really easy setup and an unblocked nickel off the edge while rushing only four. Second and long, third and long, fourth and long, any time you want pressure without taking anyone out of coverage.

plays.name: 2 Invert Lurk

reads.label: Looks Like Cover 2, Then Inverts
reads.text: Pre snap it is just normal Cover 2. Once the ball is snapped we invert it: the safety comes down and plays more like a robber in the seam in the middle of the field, and the picture changes on him. Keep the user safety back so it shows two high until the snap.

reads.label: Read Deep to Short
reads.text: You are the high safety in the hook curl. Is anything taking me deep? No. Now get aggressive and help anywhere. Anything attacking the seam, sit right on it, because you are already at depth like another deep defender.

reads.label: Play the Sticks on Fourth and Long
reads.text: Coverage, then Play the Sticks. Now the flat defenders play at sixteen yards and nothing gets over their heads. A corner route at the sticks got skied and picked on fourth and sixteen.

reads.label: Run to Your Side
reads.text: Because you are the safety, a run to your side lets you fly downhill and get super aggressive. Three yard loss on an outside toss.

adjustments: No setup, it looks like normal Cover 2
User the high safety in the hook curl and keep him back so it shows two high
Shade up or down as you like
Fourth and long: Coverage, then Play the Sticks
plays.whenToUse: The safe coverage with a disguise built in. Mix it in with the match coverages and the blitzes as one more look, and lean on it when you just want to play a nice safe shell and read deep to short.

plays.name: Pounder

reads.label: Man Under, Quarters Over the Top
reads.text: Treat it like Cover 2 Man with the two high safeties playing quarters. In the game files those two are supposed to play match, but a lot of the time they play more like drop zone, so user one of them and play him with quarters rules yourself.

reads.label: The Middle of the Field
reads.text: In Cover 2 Man the safeties get pulled outside in deep halves to help on the outside players. Here they focus on the middle of the field, the tight end and the slot receivers, where people want to throw the ball anyway.

reads.label: Get Aggressive With the User
reads.text: Play action, and the user safety comes down on it. Then it is the deep crosser: get out underneath it and take it away, while the non user safety caps the vertical routes from the interior, even out of bunch. We stepped in front for a knockout at the catch point on fourth and twenty three.

reads.label: Still Rushing Four
reads.text: It is a very good coverage defense, but we are not dropping everybody out. The front four still get home, so he does not have all day to hold it against the man coverage.

reads.label: Both Safeties in the Run Fit
reads.text: Because the safeties are in quarters they are in run fits, which they are not in Cover 2 Man. So it is two man under with much better run defense. Fire into the ball with the safety and hold it to two.

adjustments: User one of the high safeties and play him with quarters rules
On play action come down with him, then get under the crosser
plays.whenToUse: Man coverage underneath with the safeties taking away the middle of the field, and both of them still in the run fit. It is basically quarters run defense while playing man, so it works against the run and the pass.

plays.name: SS Sim 2

reads.label: Four Rushers, Pressure off the Edge
reads.text: One, two, three, four. Only four rushing, and two came free before he could even hit the back of his drop off play action. It still lets us drop everybody else out.

reads.label: A Different Look Behind It
reads.text: Instead of the Cover 3 behind Nickel Sim 2 and SS Dog 3, this is a Cover 2 invert with match principles: a seam flat, a mid read and a cloud flat. Same pressure, a different picture for the quarterback.

reads.label: Look for the Hot
reads.text: When we expect unblocked pressure, the user starts looking for hots. Two guys dropping to one side, you are responsible for the other. See the quick out, jump it, pass break up at the catch point.

reads.label: The Tackle Drops Too
reads.text: The defensive tackle drops into the hook curl on one side while the mid read sits in the middle, so your hot is the other way. On the goal line the tight end came underneath, the linebacker in the mid jumped it, and we picked it right before the half.

adjustments: The safety auto walks down; whatever side he walks down to, shift the D-line to that side
User the linebacker on the same side as the blitzer, stand him over the tackle, and blitz him
Hover just long enough to make the tackle come down inside, then get out
Shade down to hard flats or leave the cloud and the seam on the field
plays.whenToUse: The change up to the Cover 3 sim pressures. The same four man heat off the edge with a really unique shell behind it, a seam flat, a cloud flat, a mid read and a hook curl, so the quarterback who has learned Nickel Sim 2 gets a different picture.

plays.name: LB Pop 0

reads.label: Two Free Rushers
reads.text: A zero man pressure, and the point of every one of these is fast, nasty pressure. Overload the protection so that even when they block extra backs and tight ends, we still get free runners. He barely hits the back of his drop before he goes down.

reads.label: Half a Second
reads.text: If he sends everybody out on one of these, he has to get the football out in half a second. Two free rushers, three on two on one side, somebody comes through every time.

reads.label: You Have the Back
reads.text: As the user you always have whoever is uncovered in man, usually the running back, sometimes a tight end or a slot. Back goes out, go out with him. Back stays in to block, somebody else comes free anyway.

reads.label: Man Across the Board
reads.text: Man coverage everywhere, so the corners have to win. He tried to hit the crosser under the pressure and Josh Jobe undercut it for a pick six, and Julian Love high pointed the deep ball off the boot.

adjustments: Shift the D-line away from the blitzing nickel
Blitz all linebackers
User the linebacker on the blitz side, the same side as the nickel
Hover and get out; you have the back
If it is not coming in, try QB contain to change the angles
plays.whenToUse: One of the zero pressures every scheme needs a few of. Fast, nasty pressure that overloads the protection, so even when they keep extra backs and tight ends in to block we still get free runners. If he sends everybody out, the ball has to be out in half a second.

plays.name: Blitz Loop 3

reads.label: Five on Three
reads.text: The nickel comes free and the looper comes up the middle. It is basically five defenders coming over three blockers, so a lot of the time a second guy sneaks through too. The backside tackle does nothing except sometimes pick up a looper.

reads.label: Not a Sim Pressure
reads.text: Sim pressures are four on five, so sometimes they get blocked up. This is five, and if they do not block the running back it comes in every single time, from the nickel or from the looper up the middle.

reads.label: The Seam Flats Match
reads.text: Leave the seam flats on the field and they match the vertical routes. Fourth and twenty seven, three guys free, he has to push it down the field and there is nothing there. Third and two or fourth and three, shade down to hard flats and take away the quick hitters.

reads.label: You Are the Only Middle Help
reads.text: As the user in the three receiver hook you are the help in the middle of the field. Hover and get out. He tries to go quick up the seam, jump to it and step in front.

adjustments: Shift the D-line to the blitz side
Blitz all linebackers
User the outside one of the two standing linebackers, leave the inside one
Seam flats stay on; on short yardage shade down to hard flats
plays.whenToUse: The pressure for when it has to come in. Five rushers, and if they send everybody out the nickel is unblocked basically every time. Long yardage with the seam flats matching behind it, and hard flats on third and two or fourth and three.
